facts.claim: Confirm your passport is valid for at least 6 months beyond the end of your trip.

Some countries won't let you enter unless your passport is valid for six months after you plan to leave that country. Some airlines also impose this rule on their own initiative. It can apply even if you're just transiting or stopping over. Getting it wrong can mean being stranded.
facts.use_note: Say 'some countries', not 'many'. Relevant to multi-stop itineraries with stopovers.

facts.claim: Allow at least 6 weeks to get your passport. Where possible, don't book flights without a valid passport.

If you change your family name because of a change in your marital status, you can choose to get a new passport or keep using your current one. The Australian Passport Office recommends booking travel in the name that's in your passport.
facts.use_note: Book the honeymoon in the name on the passport you will carry.

facts.claim: Get the right visa for countries you're visiting or transiting through. Visa conditions often change, so check with the embassy or consulate of your destinations before every trip.

It's your responsibility to make sure you have the right visa. Visa rules can change at short notice. Contact the embassy or consulate of the country you'll be visiting; Smartraveller cannot tell you what visa to get.
facts.use_note: Confirming authority is each destination's embassy or consulate, not Wedded Wonderland.

facts.claim: Some countries ask you to give your passport to their officials for visa processing, during which you won't have your passport and can't travel anywhere else. Don't leave your application to the last minute.

Photocopy your passport ID page, visa and key documents. Take a copy with you and leave one with someone you trust. Have hard copies of online flight, accommodation and event bookings. Share your itinerary with friends or family members.
facts.use_note: Directly supports the 'share your itinerary' line in the template.

facts.claim: Talk to your doctor, find out if there are any health risks where you're going, get a basic health check at least 8 weeks before you go, and get the recommended vaccinations.
facts.use_note: Cite the Smartraveller checklist, not its outbound vaccinations link (non-government).

facts.claim: Check if your medication is legal and available where you're going. Take enough of your prescribed medicines to last the whole trip. Carry copies of your prescription and a letter from your doctor.
Smartraveller says the right travel insurance is as essential as a passport for overseas travel, for every traveller.
Choose a policy covering every country on the trip including stopovers and transit points, and check whether cancellation is covered if the advice level rises after booking.
facts.use_note: Key for a two-stop sample itinerary.

facts.claim: Insurers exclude many activities from standard policies (even common ones such as cruises); check the included and excluded activities list.
facts.use_note: Diving, snorkelling and excursions in a sample itinerary: check the activities list.

facts.claim: Always read the Product Disclosure Statement (PDS) before buying travel insurance. Travel insurance can cover cancellation costs if plans change; basic medical-only policies usually do not cover cancellation or property.
Medical assistance is usually the highest unexpected cost for Australians overseas, and the Australian Government cannot pay travellers' bills.
Travellers must tell their insurer about all pre-existing health conditions; most policies have an age limit.
Smartraveller no longer asks you to register your trip; instead you can subscribe to get email updates and alerts, and it encourages subscribing as soon as you are thinking about heading overseas.
facts.use_note: Say 'subscribe', never 'register'.

facts.claim: Australians, including dual nationals, should depart and enter Australia on their Australian passport.

A weekly itinerary template sets out each day of a trip by time of day, with stays, transfers, reservations and notes in one place. The columns that matter are the day and date, morning, afternoon and evening, where you are staying, how you move between places, what is reserved and a line of notes. Confirmation numbers, meeting points and a driver's contact belong in the notes column.
facts.use_note: Our own sister guide (published 2026-11-18). Reuse the column logic so the two templates match; link to it, do not copy the table.

facts.claim: Pacing principles on our weekly template: keep the first day light; limit each day to two core experiences (one is often enough); build in a rest day or half-day around the middle of the week; leave the final morning open; allow for jet lag on long-haul trips by keeping the first two days relatively gentle and scheduling more demanding activities from the third day onwards; keep transfer days flexible when moving between two accommodation bases.
facts.use_note: House planning guidance, not an official health source. Present jet lag pacing as our planning approach, not medical advice.

facts.claim: Booking order on our weekly template: stays first (during peak periods sought-after rooms can be reserved six to twelve months in advance), then flights and transfers, then private experiences (two to three months ahead in high season), then restaurants (often two to four weeks in advance). These are indicative planning windows rather than fixed requirements; lead times vary by destination, season and experience.
facts.use_note: Brand editorial guidance, not a supplier or official source. Keep the 'indicative' caveat. Consistent with F-28 (6 to 9 months for a honeymoon).

facts.claim: For a honeymoon, we favour slower mornings, longer evenings and opportunities to enjoy the property itself, rather than treating every day as an opportunity to explore. For a multi-stop trip, we recommend allowing a dedicated transfer day whenever the accommodation base changes.

Keep all travel arrangements in one shared document that both travellers can access from their phones, with an offline copy available before departure. Include booking confirmation numbers, transfer details, driver contact information and accommodation addresses; where useful, save property addresses in the local language.
facts.use_note: Pairs with Smartraveller F-08 (hard copies, share itinerary).

facts.claim: The /travel page lists the honeymoon as a scope: 'One place or several, straight after or months later, with the transitions handled.'
facts.page_wording: The honeymoon. One place or several, straight after or months later, with the transitions handled.

facts.claim: We plan it as one connected journey rather than a stack of separate bookings, and we stay reachable while you are away. When a flight moves or a plan changes, you message your travel agent, not a call centre queue.
facts.page_wording: We plan it as one connected journey rather than a stack of separate bookings, and we stay reachable while you are away. ... A person, not a portal. When a flight moves or a plan changes, you message your travel agent - not a call centre queue.

facts.claim: Eligible stays may include daily breakfast, a hotel credit, upgrade priority, early check-in and late checkout, a welcome amenity, preferred rates, VIP recognition and extras such as transfers or spa access. Inclusions vary by hotel, rate and dates and are confirmed in writing before you book. Upgrades and extended check-in or checkout generally depend on how full the hotel is that day.
facts.use_note: Always 'may include'. Do not attach any perk to a named hotel in the sample.

facts.claim: A straightforward hotel booking usually carries no planning fee. More complex itineraries, flights or group work may carry a fee, agreed with you upfront before any work begins.
facts.use_note: Quote exactly. A two-week multi-stop honeymoon may count as a 'more complex itinerary'. No amount published.

facts.claim: For a honeymoon, 6-9 months is ideal to lock in the right suite category (12-18 months for a destination wedding).
facts.use_note: Cite /destination-packages; not found on /destination-honeymoon-packages on 2026-11-16.

facts.claim: Hand-picked sanctuaries across the Maldives, Bali, Santorini and beyond. Our concierge curates your honeymoon anywhere in the world, for the first days of forever.

Every package is fully curated: the suite category, transfers, private dining, spa rituals, sunset experiences and the small details that turn a stay into the honeymoon you'll talk about for years, all coordinated by one team, so you arrive to a trip that just runs.
facts.use_note: Wording has CHANGED since 2026-11-16 (then: 'airport transfers, signature dining experiences, a spa ritual or two, and at least one private excursion'; honeymoon-planner F-034). Use today's wording only, or just link the page. Original uses an em dash before 'all coordinated'; replaced with a comma here.

facts.claim: Five steps on the honeymoon page: share your vision (travel window and the kind of trip you picture, barefoot and unplugged, or multi-stop and adventurous); meet your specialist; choose your escape from a tailored shortlist with suite categories and inclusions made clear; leave the details to us (transfers, dining, spa rituals, private experiences coordinated end to end); arrive and unwind, every reservation in place.
facts.use_note: 'Specialist who has stayed at these properties' is still on the page; brand self-claim awaiting Nic (honeymoon-planner N-006). Do not repeat it.

facts.claim: Honeymoon journeys: guided multi-stop journeys for couples who want to explore together. Pick one and we'll send dates, hotel options and the full day-by-day plan.
facts.use_note: Natural hub CTA for a day-by-day itinerary article. Operator of the guided journeys still unconfirmed (honeymoon-planner N-007). Do not name or count journeys, and do not lift durations or routes from the catalogue into the sample.

facts.claim: See your doctor 6 to 8 weeks before you go. You need enough time to act on their advice. Ask what travel vaccinations they suggest, and ask how to protect yourself against risks like blood clots (deep vein thrombosis) during long-haul travel.
facts.use_note: CONFLICT in wording across two Smartraveller pages, same update date: travel-health says '6 to 8 weeks', the essentials checklist says 'at least 8 weeks' (F-09). Safe line: 'book a doctor's visit at least 8 weeks before you fly' and cite the checklist, or say 'about two months'.

facts.claim: You can't access Medicare and the Pharmaceutical Benefits Scheme (PBS) overseas. Hospital stays overseas often cost thousands of dollars per day. Costs can also include loss of prepaid activities, cancellation fees for booked activities, flights or accommodation, and flight changes.
facts.use_note: Not a price; government statement. No Nic sign-off needed.

facts.claim: Take action to prevent blood clots caused by long-haul travel. Take a small first aid kit, including SPF 30-50+ sunscreen and insect repellent. Ideally, take enough medicine for your whole trip; your medicine may not be available or legal where you're going.

Basic travel insurance policies don't cover you for higher-risk activities; some will only cover your activity if you pay extra. Look into any tour or service providers you're using and ensure they have a good reputation.
facts.use_note: Pairs with F-13.

legal.summary: Passport valid at least 6 months beyond the end of the trip.
Some countries and airlines apply a six-month validity rule, including in transit.
legal.authority: Smartraveller (DFAT); confirm with each destination's embassy or consulate

legal.summary: Allow at least 6 weeks for a passport; avoid booking flights without one.
Married name change: new passport optional; book travel in the passport name.
Correct visa for every country visited or transited; check with the embassy or consulate before every trip.
Visa is the traveller's responsibility; rules change at short notice; Smartraveller cannot advise which visa.
Some visa processes hold the passport; apply early.
Australians, including dual nationals, depart and enter Australia on their Australian passport.
